- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.23) — model tends to overshoot bullish momentum.
- Underestimate late-period spikes (last 5–7 days of forecast) when sentiment turns negative or neutral — model fails to capture reversal or volatility tail.
- Lag in price correction after sharp sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to negative sentiment, often missing downward momentum.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust downward when sentiment turns negative, especially after 10–15 day windows.
- Overshoot after spikes: model forecasts peak prices too high after strong sentiment rallies, then undercorrects in subsequent days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then underestimate later spikes (last 10–15 days) when sentiment turns neutral or negative.
